questions.question: Describe the Moon and explain why it shines at night.
questions.expected_answer: The Moon is a ball of rock covered with craters and grey dust. It has dark patches, which are plains of dark rock, and brighter higher land. It does not make its own light. It shines because sunlight falls on it and bounces off towards us.

questions.question: Explain why nothing can live on the Moon.
questions.expected_answer: The Moon has no air to breathe and no liquid water like the Earth's. It also gets extremely hot in the sunshine and extremely cold in the dark, because there is no air to act like a blanket. Living things need air, water and a steady temperature, so nothing can live there.

questions.question: Compare the Moon to the Earth and the Sun in size and distance.
questions.expected_answer: The Moon is much smaller than the Earth, only about a quarter as wide. It is much closer to the Earth than the Sun is, about three hundred and eighty-four thousand kilometres away. The Sun is much bigger than both, and about four hundred times further away than the Moon.
